sentences.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption commissioned a telephone survey of 500 NSW residents in April 2003 to examine public views of corruption and ICAC.
sentences.support:
The survey was conducted by telephone within a two week period in April, 
2003.

sentences.text: It examined perceived corruption and its effects, attitudes to reporting, and awareness and perceptions of ICAC, with comparisons to earlier surveys.
sentences.support:
This document provides a brief summary of the findings of the 2003 survey, 
including some comparisons with the findings of previous surveys.

sentences.text: ICAC reported that 82% perceived corruption as a problem in NSW, while 97% supported reporting it and 89% believed individuals had a responsibility to report.
sentences.support:
most respondents believing it is OK to 
report corruption (97%) and that individuals have a responsibility to report 
corruption (89%).

sentences.text: ICAC also reported that 71% said they would probably report corruption, but only 34% knew where to report it.
sentences.support:
only a third (34%) said they knew where to report 
corruption in the NSW public sector.

findings.quote:
Public cynicism about the outcomes of reporting corruption appears to be 
waning.

There was also evidence of improving confidence that people who report 
corruption will not suffer negative consequences.

notes: Findings describe respondents' attitudes and reported experiences rather than established misconduct. No numbered recommendations list.
